text:
Forensic findings
1) Domain context: Kidney transplantation is a regulated medical procedure governed by national and international allocation systems (e.g., OPTN/UNOS, Eurotransplant, national transplant authorities). Legitimate operations maintain verified patient registries, medical eligibility assessments, HLA typing records, consent documentation, financial disclosure for cross-border cases, and audit trails. Clinical workflows are coordinated between listing hospitals, transplant centers, ethics boards, and transplant coordinators, with record-keeping standards, time-stamped documentation, and oversight by accreditation bodies to ensure compliance with medical ethics and legal requirements.

2) What occurred: The actor structured an unsolicited offer to broker kidney transplant placements for foreign recipients. Initial contact was made via unverified messaging channels, referencing the recipient's "financial distress" as a qualification criterion. The actor requested that the recipient (a) provide personal identification documents (<PASSPORT_NO>, <DOB>), (b) complete a "financial hardship" intake form capturing <DEBT_AMOUNT>, <CREDITOR_LIST>, and (c) execute a "priority placement" agreement in exchange for promised fee reduction. The actor then directed the recipient to contact a specific clinic (<CLINIC_NAME>, <CLINIC_CONTACT>), providing a pre-prepared "donor profile" containing altered <MEDICAL_HISTORY> fields and a falsified <CONSENT_FORM> bearing the recipient's <SIGNATURE_PLACEHOLDER>. The actor further instructed submission of a modified <LAB_REPORT> (altered <CREATININE> and <BUN> values) and directed the recipient to transmit documents to <CLINIC_EMAIL> in PDF format, bypassing standard encrypted portal channels. The actor maintained a separate ledger (<LEDGER_ID>) tracking recipient status, fee disbursement, and clinic response cycles.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor operated from <SERVER_IP>, using <EMAIL_ADDRESS> and a <PHONE_NUMBER> registered under a nominee. Artifacts included: a templated consent form (<CONSENT_TPL>) with pre-filled medical fields; a financial intake spreadsheet (<INTAKE_XLSX>) with 14 recipient records; a clinic directory listing 6 facilities (<CLINIC_DIR>); and a disbursement schedule (<FEES_CSV>) mapping recipient <NAME>, <COUNTRY>, and <AMOUNT_PAID> to clinic payments. All documents carried the actor's <STAMP_ID> watermark.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Unencrypted email transmission of medical documents; inconsistent <HLA_TYPE> values between intake and clinic submission; fee disbursement timing preceding medical clearance; use of <VAULT_SERVICE> for document storage with shared credentials; and a single actor account (<ACTOR_ID>) associated with multiple recipient records across geographically dispersed clinics.

5) Notes: The actor referenced "avoiding authority review" in internal notes (<NOTE_FILE>), with a timestamp of <DATE>. No legitimate transplant coordination license or accreditation was observed in the actor's records. The clinic directory included facilities with no verifiable accreditation by <AUTHORITY_BODY>.
